As a little sanctuary

It would come immediately

answers: Evil or wrongdoing
Joy
Prayer

They believed the city was empty
They believed the city belonged to the exiles

As men who devised mischief and gave wicked counsel
As men asking to leave the city

paragraphs.title: Judgment on the Leaders and the Sword

answers: Against the exiles
Against the leaders of the city
Against the cherubim
easy.explanation: Ezekiel was commanded to prophesy against the men who led the city.
easy.q: Against whom was Ezekiel commanded to prophesy?

answers: Violence and killing
Building houses
Scattering among the countries
easy.explanation: They had multiplied the slain and filled the streets with the slain.
easy.q: What were the city's leaders accused of doing?

answers: Peace
A sanctuary
A sword
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will bring a sword upon you.”
easy.q: What would be brought upon the leaders?

answers: Because they would be brought out of it
Because it would be emptied of leaders without judgment
Because they would move into the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The Lord said He would bring them out of the midst of the city.
medium.q: Why would the city not be a caldron for the leaders?

answers: They would remain in the city, build houses, and be saved
They would be brought out, delivered to strangers, and fall by the sword
They would return to the exiles, cleanse the land, and receive a new heart

medium.q: What sequence of consequences was announced to the leaders?

answers: People who had been killed
People who had escaped
People who had prayed

It caused him to leave the exiles immediately

The sword symbolized protection for the city
The sword was given to the exiles so they could return

challenge.q: What is the connection between the sword the leaders feared and the judgment upon them?

They had multiplied killing and followed the ways of the heathen instead of the Lord's statutes and judgments
They had lived in other countries
challenge.explanation: They had shed blood and followed the manners of the heathen rather than the Lord's ways.
challenge.q: What moral reason is given for the leaders' judgment?

paragraphs.title: The Exiles as a Little Sanctuary

answers: Only the people of Jerusalem
The exiles and all the house of Israel
Only the city's leaders
easy.explanation: The Lord identified Ezekiel's brethren as the men of his kindred and all the house of Israel.
easy.q: Who were Ezekiel's “brethren” according to the word of the Lord?

answers: That they were near to the Lord
That they should become leaders
That they should get far from the Lord and that the land had been given to them
easy.explanation: The inhabitants of Jerusalem told the exiles to get far from the Lord and claimed the land for themselves.
easy.q: What did the inhabitants of Jerusalem say about the exiles?

answers: A little sanctuary
The city gate
A caldron of flesh
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will be to them as a little sanctuary.”
easy.q: What was the Lord to the exiles in the countries where they came?

answers: Jerusalem's inhabitants reject the exiles, while the Lord recognizes them as part of Israel
Jerusalem's inhabitants welcome the exiles, while the Lord rejects them
Both groups claim that the land does not belong to Israel
medium.explanation: Jerusalem's inhabitants reject the exiles, but the Lord calls them brethren and part of all Israel.
medium.q: What contrast is shown between the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the exiles?

answers: He remains present with them even though they are distant and scattered
They built a large temple in every country
They had already returned to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Though scattered among the countries, the Lord Himself was their place of holiness and refuge.
medium.q: Why is it significant that the Lord is called a “little sanctuary” for the exiles?

answers: A small sacred place or a sanctifying presence among the exiles
A small gate in Jerusalem
A country without inhabitants

medium.q: What does “a little sanctuary” mean in this context?

answers: Only those in Jerusalem belong to Israel
The exiles, though distant and scattered, also belong to the house of Israel

answers: It shows that the exiles are not part of the people

challenge.q: How does the Lord's answer challenge Jerusalem's claim concerning the land?

answers: Their scattering prevents any relationship with the Lord
While scattered among the countries, the Lord Himself is their little sanctuary
Their scattering makes them belong only to the nations
challenge.explanation: The passage connects their scattering among the countries with the Lord's presence as their little sanctuary.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the exiles' scattering and the little sanctuary?

medium.q: What connection is made between the new heart and keeping the Lord's ways?

answers: Scattering, sword, and death
Gathering, cleansing, a changed heart, and obedience to the Lord
Leaving the land, building a city, and making war
medium.explanation: The Lord promises to gather the people, remove abominations, give them a new heart, and lead them in His ways.
medium.q: What is the main sequence of promises in these verses?

answers: A hard heart that does not turn to the Lord
A heart filled with unusual joy
A heart belonging only to the city's leaders

answers: A change only in the city's leaders

A change in the location of the east gate

challenge.q: What contrast is shown between those with the new heart and those who follow abominations?
